subject: Art & Design
source: National Curriculum (Art and Design). Drive Art & Design folder reviewed (Elements of Art deck, KS3 files) and the school's 'Art - Y9' lesson plan example used for format and the Y9 Zentangle topic.

lessons.title: Colour theory: the colour wheel and mood
objectives: Explain warm and cool colours and complementary pairs
Use colour to create a mood

keywords.def: red, yellow and blue: colours that cannot be made by mixing
colours made by mixing two primaries: orange, green, purple
colours like red, orange and yellow that feel hot
colours opposite each other on the wheel, such as blue and orange

starter: Bismillah. Name the three primary colours.

teach.heading: The colour wheel
bullets: Colours sit in a circle in order
teach.note: Pupils need colouring pencils or paint, paper, a pencil. Show a colour wheel on screen. Pupils draw a circle and divide into six.

teach.heading: Mixing secondaries
teach.note: If using pencils, layer lightly. Misconception: mixing always makes brown; this happens with too many colours.

teach.heading: Warm and cool
teach.note: Ask pupils to sort items: sun, ice, forest, fire. Show how complementary pairs create contrast.

teach.heading: Colour and mood
teach.note: Link to calm and wellbeing; mention Allah's creation of sunsets. Do not use faces.

teach.heading: Planning a mood picture
teach.note: Abstract shapes: circles, waves, triangles. Pupils choose a mood word.

practice: Mix red and blue. What colour?
independent: Complete a six-colour wheel and label primary and secondary colours.
Sort six objects into warm and cool lists.
exit: Create an abstract picture using only warm colours; then one using only cool colours.
Write a sentence about the mood of each.
homework: What mood do cool colours give?
lessons.send: Find three warm and three cool colours in your home and list them.

lessons.title: Symmetry and design: a four-fold tile
objectives: Draw a design that is symmetrical in four sections
Use a plant shape as inspiration

keywords.def: when one side is a mirror image of the other
the line you can fold along to make two matching halves
a single design that can be repeated
a flowing design based on plants and curves

starter: Name a warm colour and a cool colour.

teach.heading: Symmetry in nature
bullets: A snowflake has many lines of symmetry
teach.note: Show a leaf. Ask for lines of symmetry. Pupils need paper, pencil, ruler, colouring pencils.

teach.heading: Arabesque designs
bullets: Used on walls, books and tiles
teach.note: Show photos of arabesque tilework. Explain that artists used curves, leaves and flowers.

teach.heading: Four equal sections
bullets: Draw a square 10 cm by 10 cm
Draw lines to split it in four
Draw a motif in one section
teach.note: Model on a board. Ask what happens if we flip the motif to each section.

teach.heading: Reflecting the design
bullets: Copy the motif as a mirror image
Do it for all four sections
The corners meet in the middle
teach.note: Common error: copying without flipping. Show with a mirror or tracing paper.

teach.heading: Colour and finish
bullets: Repeat the same colour in matching places
teach.note: Remind them of the colour wheel. Matching colours keep the symmetry.

practice: Draw one line of symmetry on a leaf.
How many lines of symmetry has a square?
independent: Draw a motif in one quarter of a square and mirror it into the next.
Check with a mirror or fold.
exit: Complete a four-fold design based on a plant shape.
Colour it using a complementary pair.
lessons.send: Design a second tile with a different motif and compare.
